title: Gostman — API client for REST, GraphQL, gRPC and WebSocket
excerpt: Free, open source API client for the browser and the desktop. No account and no paid tier: tests, a CI command line, a mock server and team sharing are all included.
content_html:
Gostman

001Workflow

Tests, the command line, Git, mocks, captured traffic, sharing and your coding agent all work from the same files.

Add checks as plain rows, or write a script with test() and expect(). The results sit beside the response, so a broken contract shows up on the request that broke it.

  • Checks on status, headers, body and response time
  • Pre-request and post-response scripts, run in a sandbox
  • A runner in the app for a whole folder at once

gostman run sends every request in a folder with its scripts, variables and cookies, prints what failed and why, and exits non-zero so the pipeline stops. There is no runtime to install.

  • Text, JSON and JUnit reports
  • Secrets passed from the environment, never stored in the collection
  • Linux, macOS and Windows builds on every release

Open a folder and every request becomes a small YAML file: one file per request, one directory per folder. Commit it next to the code it tests and review changes line by line.

  • Tokens, cookies and history never reach the folder
  • A cloned folder runs no scripts until you trust it
  • The app, the command line and your agent all read the same files

Save any response as an example, then start a local server that answers each route with it. Build the frontend before the API exists, and watch every request it makes arrive in the log.

  • Pick which example each route returns while the server runs
  • Optional delay and CORS for browser clients
  • Also available as gostman mock and to agents over MCP

Point your app at a local address and Gostman forwards every call to your API while listing each one live. Save any of them as a request, with its response kept as an example. There is no certificate to install.

  • Works for any app whose API base URL you can change
  • Authorization and cookie headers are never saved
  • In the desktop app and as gostman capture

Send a folder as an encrypted link or file that is built in your own window and never uploaded, or turn the collection into a single documentation page you can host anywhere.

  • Variable values and saved responses stay out unless you include them
  • The recipient sees what is inside before importing
  • One self-contained HTML file, from the app or gostman docs

Claude Code, Codex and Cursor can call Gostman through MCP in place of curl. They use the collection you already have, and variable values and credentials are filled in inside Gostman and replaced with their names in everything the agent reads.

  • Cookies, tokens and variables carry across calls in a session
  • Responses are capped and can be narrowed to the fields that matter
  • Agents reach only the hosts your collection already uses, unless you allow more

002Download

Gostman is open source. Every feature below is included, with no licence key and no seat count.

Every protocol
REST, GraphQL with a schema browser, gRPC through reflection or .proto files, WebSocket, Socket.IO, MQTT, Server-Sent Events, SOAP and MCP in one window.

Auth for real APIs
Basic, bearer, API key, OAuth 1 and 2 with renewal, Digest, AWS SigV4, NTLM, Akamai EdgeGrid, JWT, ASAP and Hawk.

Bodies and transport
JSON, XML, form, multipart and file bodies, a cookie jar, proxy and client certificates, and curl commands pasted straight into a request.

Responses
JSON tree, HTML, image and PDF previews, headers, cookies, size and timing. Download any body, including binary, or copy it as code in 13 languages, including cURL, Python, Go, Java, C#, Swift and Rust.

Variables done properly
Secret variables in your OS keychain, plus global, collection, folder and request scopes, dynamic variables and prompts.

Secret managers
Pull values from Vault, AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, 1Password, Bitwarden or KeePassXC at send time.

A runner built for CI
CSV and JSON data, parallel runs, HTML and JUnit reports, and a CLI that exits non-zero on failure.

Mock server
Serve saved examples or an OpenAPI spec locally, with rules and a live request log.

A real Git panel
Diff, commit, push, branches, stash and conflict resolution, in the desktop app.

Plain files
Nested collections, tabs and history, kept as plain YAML files in a folder or in app storage.

Import and export
Import Postman, OpenAPI, Insomnia, HAR, WSDL, Bruno collections, .http files and curl commands. Export to Postman, OpenAPI, Markdown, .http files or a backup.

Agent-ready, and in the browser
An MCP server with secret redaction and a host allowlist, and a web version with nothing to install.

AI features, bring your own key
Off by default, and hidden while off. Bring your own key for Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, OpenRouter, Ollama, LM Studio or any compatible URL. Keys stay on your device, in the OS keychain on desktop, and each request is previewed with secrets masked unless you turn the preview off.

Who is Gostman for?

Developers and testers who want their API collections kept as files next to the code: backend developers checking their own endpoints, frontend developers working against a mock before the API exists, QA engineers running API tests in CI, and teams that review request changes in pull requests. It also suits teams that cannot keep collections in a vendor's cloud, and people who want their coding agent to use the same requests. It is not the right tool if you need hosted collaboration, single sign-on or scheduled cloud monitors, because Gostman has no accounts.

Is Gostman free?

Yes. Gostman is open source under the MIT licence. Every feature is in the download, with no account, no licence key and no seat count.

Will Gostman add a paid tier?

Gostman has no paid tier, no account and no licence key, and every feature is in the free download. It is released under the MIT licence, so the published code stays free to use, change and fork whatever happens to the project.

What happens to my collections if Gostman stops being developed?

They keep working. A folder workspace is plain YAML in your own repository, the desktop app and the command line need no Gostman server, and collections export to Postman, Bruno, OpenAPI, HAR and .http files. The MIT licence also lets anyone fork the code and carry it on.

Where are my collections kept?

On your machine. The desktop app keeps them in its data folder or in a folder of YAML files you choose, and the web version keeps them in your browser's storage. Nothing is synced to a Gostman server.

Does the web version send my requests through a server?

By default, yes. Browsers cannot call most APIs directly, so the web version relays each request through a small hosted proxy that stores neither the request nor the response and cannot reach localhost or private addresses. To reach those, run gostman relay on your computer and choose it in the web app's preferences, or use the desktop app, which sends requests from your own machine.

Can I bring my Postman or Bruno collections?

Yes. Import Postman, Bruno (.bru files or the YAML format), Insomnia, OpenAPI, HAR, .http files and curl. Common pm.* and bru.* script calls are rewritten to Gostman's script API. An import only adds data, and it lists any scripts it carries before you accept them.

How does a team share a collection?

Open a folder and commit it with your code: one YAML file per request, reviewed in pull requests like any other change. For a quick hand-off, send an encrypted share link that is built in your window and never uploaded.

Can it run in CI?

Yes. gostman run sends a folder with its scripts and assertions, prints what failed and exits non-zero, with text, JSON, JUnit and HTML reports. The repository includes a GitHub Action and a Dockerfile.

005Integrations

Import from other clients, read secrets from your vault, run checks in any CI and hand requests to your coding agent.

  • Postman
  • Claude Code
  • GitHub Actions
  • OpenAPI
  • HashiCorp Vault
  • Cursor
  • Insomnia
  • Docker
  • Bruno
  • OpenAI
  • GitHub
  • 1Password
  • GitLab
  • AWS Secrets Manager
  • Linux
  • macOS
  • Windows
  • Azure Key Vault
  • Bitwarden
  • Google Cloud Secret Manager
  • Gemini
  • KeePassXC
  • Ollama
  • Bitbucket
  • OpenRouter

Download the desktop app for Windows, macOS or Linux, or open the web version now. There is nothing to sign up for.

Free and open source · macOS, Windows, and Linux · No account

content_html_zh:
Gostman

001Workflow

Tests, the command line, Git, mocks, captured traffic, sharing and your coding agent all work from the same files.

Add checks as plain rows, or write a script with test() and expect(). The results sit beside the response, so a broken contract shows up on the request that broke it.

  • Checks on status, headers, body and response time
  • Pre-request and post-response scripts, run in a sandbox
  • A runner in the app for a whole folder at once

gostman run sends every request in a folder with its scripts, variables and cookies, prints what failed and why, and exits non-zero so the pipeline stops. There is no runtime to install.

  • Text, JSON and JUnit reports
  • Secrets passed from the environment, never stored in the collection
  • Linux, macOS and Windows builds on every release

Open a folder and every request becomes a small YAML file: one file per request, one directory per folder. Commit it next to the code it tests and review changes line by line.

  • Tokens, cookies and history never reach the folder
  • A cloned folder runs no scripts until you trust it
  • The app, the command line and your agent all read the same files

Save any response as an example, then start a local server that answers each route with it. Build the frontend before the API exists, and watch every request it makes arrive in the log.

  • Pick which example each route returns while the server runs
  • Optional delay and CORS for browser clients
  • Also available as gostman mock and to agents over MCP

Point your app at a local address and Gostman forwards every call to your API while listing each one live. Save any of them as a request, with its response kept as an example. There is no certificate to install.

  • Works for any app whose API base URL you can change
  • Authorization and cookie headers are never saved
  • In the desktop app and as gostman capture

Send a folder as an encrypted link or file that is built in your own window and never uploaded, or turn the collection into a single documentation page you can host anywhere.

  • Variable values and saved responses stay out unless you include them
  • The recipient sees what is inside before importing
  • One self-contained HTML file, from the app or gostman docs

Claude Code, Codex and Cursor can call Gostman through MCP in place of curl. They use the collection you already have, and variable values and credentials are filled in inside Gostman and replaced with their names in everything the agent reads.

  • Cookies, tokens and variables carry across calls in a session
  • Responses are capped and can be narrowed to the fields that matter
  • Agents reach only the hosts your collection already uses, unless you allow more

002Download

Gostman is open source. Every feature below is included, with no licence key and no seat count.

Every protocolREST, GraphQL with a schema browser, gRPC through reflection or .proto files, WebSocket, Socket.IO, MQTT, Server-Sent Events, SOAP and MCP in one window.

Auth for real APIsBasic, bearer, API key, OAuth 1 and 2 with renewal, Digest, AWS SigV4, NTLM, Akamai EdgeGrid, JWT, ASAP and Hawk.

Bodies and transportJSON, XML, form, multipart and file bodies, a cookie jar, proxy and client certificates, and curl commands pasted straight into a request.

ResponsesJSON tree, HTML, image and PDF previews, headers, cookies, size and timing. Download any body, including binary, or copy it as code in 13 languages, including cURL, Python, Go, Java, C#, Swift and Rust.

Variables done properlySecret variables in your OS keychain, plus global, collection, folder and request scopes, dynamic variables and prompts.

Secret managersPull values from Vault, AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, 1Password, Bitwarden or KeePassXC at send time.

A runner built for CICSV and JSON data, parallel runs, HTML and JUnit reports, and a CLI that exits non-zero on failure.

Mock serverServe saved examples or an OpenAPI spec locally, with rules and a live request log.

A real Git panelDiff, commit, push, branches, stash and conflict resolution, in the desktop app.

Who is Gostman for?

Developers and testers who want their API collections kept as files next to the code: backend developers checking their own endpoints, frontend developers working against a mock before the API exists, QA engineers running API tests in CI, and teams that review request changes in pull requests. It also suits teams that cannot keep collections in a vendor's cloud, and people who want their coding agent to use the same requests. It is not the right tool if you need hosted collaboration, single sign-on or scheduled cloud monitors, because Gostman has no accounts.

Is Gostman free?

是的。 Gostman is open source under the MIT licence. Every feature is in the download, with no account, no licence key and no seat count.

Will Gostman add a paid tier?

Gostman has no paid tier, no account and no licence key, and every feature is in the free download. It is released under the MIT licence, so the published code stays free to use, change and fork whatever happens to the project.

What happens to my collections if Gostman stops being developed?

They keep working. A folder workspace is plain YAML in your own repository, the desktop app and the command line need no Gostman server, and collections export to Postman, Bruno, OpenAPI, HAR and .http files. The MIT licence also lets anyone fork the code and carry it on.

Where are my collections kept?

On your machine. The desktop app keeps them in its data folder or in a folder of YAML files you choose, and the web version keeps them in your browser's storage. Nothing is synced to a Gostman server.

Does the web version send my requests through a server?

By default, yes. Browsers cannot call most APIs directly, so the web version relays each request through a small hosted proxy that stores neither the request nor the response and cannot reach localhost or private addresses. To reach those, run gostman relay on your computer and choose it in the web app's preferences, or use the desktop app, which sends requests from your own machine.

Can I bring my Postman or Bruno collections?

是的。 Import Postman, Bruno (.bru files or the YAML format), Insomnia, OpenAPI, HAR, .http files and curl. Common pm.* and bru.* script calls are rewritten to Gostman's script API. An import only adds data, and it lists any scripts it carries before you accept them.

How does a team share a collection?

Open a folder and commit it with your code: one YAML file per request, reviewed in pull requests like any other change. For a quick hand-off, send an encrypted share link that is built in your window and never uploaded.

Can it run in CI?

是的。 gostman run sends a folder with its scripts and assertions, prints what failed and exits non-zero, with text, JSON, JUnit and HTML reports. The repository includes a GitHub Action and a Dockerfile.

005Integrations

Import from other clients, read secrets from your vault, run checks in any CI and hand requests to your coding agent.
